To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the frequency of miniature endplate potentials was increased by agents that potentiated the release of acetylcholine from nerve terminals.

the frequency of spontaneous transmitter release from nerve terminals is increased in dystrophic mice and that this increase is probably due to the inability of the nerve terminal to regulate the intracellular concentration of calcium ions.
the nerve‐terminal regulation and the sensitivity of the nerve terminals to extracellular calcium ions are altered in dystrophic mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of dystrophy on the neuromuscular system.
the effects of muscular dystrophy in the mouse on nerve terminals of skeletal muscles.
the regulation of spontaneous transmitter release in skeletal muscle of normal and dystrophic mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nerve terminals of the dystrophic mouse are more susceptible to the effects of increased calcium ion concentration than are the nerve terminals of normal mice.

the nerve terminals of muscles from dystrophic animals are more sensitive to the effects of a variety of agents that alter intraterminal calcium ion concentration than are the terminals of normal muscles.
the nerve‐terminal regulation is more efficient in normal muscles and that the efficiency of this regulation is reduced in dystrophic muscles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nerve terminal's regulation of intracellular free ionized calcium is altered in dystrophic muscles.
the nerve terminal of dystrophic slow‐muscle fibres is more excitable than normal, and that the nerve terminal's excitation threshold in fast‐twitch fibres is also reduced.
the dystrophic mouse nerve terminal is less efficient than that of the normal mouse in maintaining the intratermial free calcium ion concentration at a low level.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MEPP frequency is an indicator of the concentration of free intraterminal calcium ions, and that the MEPP rate is a useful tool for investigating the mechanisms of neuromuscular transmission.
dystrophic muscles are more susceptible to the effects of agents which alter calcium ion homeostasis.

the dystrophic muscle's nerve terminals are more sensitive to changes in intracellular free calcium concentration, and thus, the MEPP frequency is a better indicator of the free calcium ion concentration at the dystrophic neuromuscular junction.
